lastText: File ClosedThe Salient, Sealed TwiceContestedAllied Combined Chiefs, 1940–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. The Strait of Messina was sealed rather than left to the Patton–Montgomery race: denying Kesselring's Italian defense some of the roughly 100,000 veteran troops it historically escaped with. The Mediterranean Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost anyway. Shingle was cancelled and the landing craft kept for Overlord: no wildcat, no stranded whale, and a Gustav Line ground down frontally instead. What was really being decided, choice by choice, was never whether Germany lost, only what the peace on the other side of it would look like.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
